messages.author: 8a16e6371f5437b9
messages.subject: bilat.symmetry
parts:
Hello everyone, I had use geomorph before, but I was on other projects and back to morphology. In a new research project I'm working with bat mites, and the analysis need to be done through a bilateral symmetry approach. I have never done anything using bilat.symmetry function and I wonder if someone could help me on how to format the file for "land.pairs" if I have 115 individuals with 14 fixed landmarks each and og those landmarks all are paired. 
Thanks for your help

messages.author: baf6eb7bae06984d
messages.subject: Re: bilat.symmetry
parts:
you just need to create a matrix that describes how landmarks are paired. E.g., if your landmarks are ordered such that 1 is on left, 2 is on right, 3 is on left 4 is on right so forth.. you can create these vectors:
left <- c(1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13)
right <-c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14)
and then assign the land.pairs to cbind(left, right)

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] bilat.symmetry
parts:
The number of rows in Mydata is not the same as the length of ind.  This appears to be because you have quotes around “imageID”, which means you are assigning ind to have a single character value, “ImageID”.  This should be a variable with the same number of values as rows in your data matrix or the third dimension in a 3-dimensional array of Procrustes coordinates.

Mike
